summary: With a LEFT JOIN, where you put a condition changes the result.
points: A condition in ON decides which right rows match, and left rows all stay.
A condition in WHERE runs after the join and removes rows, including unmatched ones.
WHERE right.column = value removes NULL rows, turning a left join into an inner join.
To filter the right table and keep every left row, put the condition in ON.

example.explanation: Every customer stays. Customers without a shipped order show NULL, including those with only other statuses.
